meta.title: Capability notes for the 25 minerals outside the owner's capability map
meta.method: Same fields and scales as the capability map. World lines from USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026; India lines from the Indian Minerals Yearbook, Department of Atomic Energy and DRDO publications, company filings and the owner's dashboard and project map; each figure was read in the cited source. Complexity is the dashboard's extraction and refining score.
meta.status: Drafted by Claude for the owner's review; not part of the workbook.

minerals.name: Antimony
minerals.next_move: Turn Hindustan Zinc's by-product stream into metal and trioxide at scale; tie up concentrate for the smelters India already runs.
minerals.what_india_has: Smelters that run on imported ore and concentrate (6,460 t in 2022-23) and export metal; Hindustan Zinc, which recovers antimony from smelter dust and slag as a by-product; high-purity antimony and antimony trioxide at the Nuclear Fuel Complex.
minerals.cost: No public plant figure found. A new mine is costly: Perpetua's Stibnite gold-antimony project in Idaho is put at US$2.2 bn.

stages.world: China 36%, Russia 29%, Tajikistan 20% of 110,000 t (2025).
stages.india: No mine output. 255 kt of contained antimony in inferred resources: Himachal Pradesh (68%) and Madhya Pradesh.

stages.world: Roasting and smelting to metal and trioxide; China has 70 to 80% of refined output.
stages.india: Smelters process imported ore; India supplied 22% of US imports of unwrought antimony in 2021-24. Hindustan Zinc recovers trioxide of over 95% purity from slag.

stages.world: Antimony trioxide for flame retardants; antimonial lead for batteries.
stages.india: Exported 22,852 t of antimonial lead and 1,590 t of antimony alloys and scrap in 2022-23; the Nuclear Fuel Complex makes high-purity antimony.

stages.world: Flame retardants, lead-acid batteries, ammunition, solar glass.
stages.india: Battery, flame-retardant and glass makers.

minerals.name: Bismuth
minerals.next_move: Recover bismuth where lead and zinc are already smelted; Hindustan Zinc says it is building that capability.
minerals.what_india_has: Bismuth occurs in Hindustan Zinc's Rajpura-Dariba lead-zinc deposit, and the company is developing in-house extraction of bismuth and other minor metals from smelter waste. The Nuclear Fuel Complex makes high-purity bismuth in small lots. No commercial production.

stages.world: A by-product of lead and tungsten ores; USGS gives no mine table.
stages.india: Present in the Rajpura-Dariba lead-zinc deposit in Rajasthan; not recovered.

stages.world: China 14,000 of 16,000 t refined (2025); South Korea 1,000 t; Japan and Laos 500 t each.
stages.india: None. Hindustan Zinc is developing extraction from smelter waste and tailings.

stages.world: Bismuth chemicals for medicines and pigments; low-melting alloys.
stages.india: The Nuclear Fuel Complex makes bismuth of over 99.99% purity for electronics; no commercial output.

stages.world: Pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, solders, lead-free alloys.
stages.india: Fully import-dependent.

minerals.name: Cadmium
minerals.next_move: Scale the cadmium recovery that Hindustan Zinc and Runaya restarted in FY2026, then add high-purity refining for solar and nuclear use.
minerals.what_india_has: 913 t/yr of installed recovery capacity at zinc smelters (Chanderiya 468, Debari 250; Vizag and Binani suspended). Hindustan Zinc made cadmium products again in FY2026 by refining purification cake with Runaya, which is adding cadmium capacity in Rajasthan.
minerals.cost: The recovery circuits exist; no public figure for high-purity refining.

stages.world: A by-product of zinc; China mines about 32% of the world's zinc.
stages.india: Hindustan Zinc's Rajasthan mines carry cadmium in their zinc ore.

stages.world: China 9,500 of 23,000 t (2025); South Korea 4,300 t; Japan and Canada 1,300 t each.
stages.india: 913 t/yr installed, 99.95% purity at Chanderiya. No output was reported after 47 t in 2017-18, until cadmium products were made again in FY2026.

stages.world: Nickel-cadmium batteries; cadmium telluride; pigments.
stages.india: The Nuclear Fuel Complex makes high-purity cadmium; Hindustan Zinc plans R&D on it.

stages.world: Industrial batteries, thin-film solar, pigments, coatings.
stages.india: Imported 6,374 t in 2021-22, mainly from South Korea, Japan and Russia; paint, glass and chemical makers, and First Solar's cadmium telluride plant.

minerals.name: Germanium
minerals.next_move: Recover germanium at Hindustan Zinc's planned tailings plant, and scale DRDO's germanium crystal growth for infrared optics.
minerals.what_india_has: Hindustan Zinc's 10 Mt/yr tailings reprocessing plant at Rampura Agucha (approved 2025) is meant to recover zinc and critical minerals including germanium; DRDO's Solid State Physics Laboratory grows optical-grade germanium crystals and lens blanks.
minerals.cost: Hindustan Zinc's tailings plant, which targets several metals, is budgeted at up to Rs 3,823 crore.

stages.world: A by-product of zinc ores; also found in lignite coal.
stages.india: Hindustan Zinc mines zinc at scale; no germanium grades are published for its ores.

stages.world: China is the leading producer; also Belgium, Canada, Germany, Russia and the US. USGS gives no tonnages.
stages.india: None yet. Hindustan Zinc's tailings plant is to recover critical minerals including germanium.

stages.world: Germanium tetrachloride for fibre; crystals, lenses and wafers.
stages.india: DRDO's laboratory grows germanium single crystals of 100 mm and more and makes lens blanks; crystals are otherwise imported.

stages.world: Fibre optics, infrared optics, satellite solar cells.
stages.india: Defence infrared optics, fibre and space; mostly imported.

minerals.name: Rhenium
minerals.next_move: Capture the rhenium that arrives in imported concentrates, put at 1.5 to 2 t a year, and recover it from spent reforming catalysts and superalloy scrap.
minerals.value_chain_step: Rhenium from copper smelting and scrap
minerals.what_india_has: No recovery (IBM records no production). A 2023 study estimates that the concentrates India processes carry 1.5 to 2 t of recoverable rhenium a year, none of it captured. Hindustan Platinum treats spent catalysts, but the metals it reports recovering do not include rhenium.
minerals.cost: No public plant figure found. USGS reports that recyclers need rhenium above US$3,000 a kilogram to cover processing costs.

stages.world: A by-product of molybdenum from copper mines: Chile 30 of 81 t (2025), China 20 t, Poland 10 t, US 9.8 t.
stages.india: None mined. Imported concentrates carry an estimated 1.5 to 2 t of recoverable rhenium a year.

stages.world: Caught from roaster and smelter gases as ammonium perrhenate. Scrap adds 20 to 25 t a year, led by the US and Germany.
stages.india: None.

stages.world: Rhenium in nickel superalloys; platinum-rhenium reforming catalysts.
stages.india: None reported.

stages.world: Turbine blades (about 80%), refinery catalysts (about 15%).
stages.india: Aero-engine programmes and refineries; all imported.

chemistry_how.k08: Spent platinum-rhenium reforming catalysts from refineries are the nearest scrap feed; Indian recyclers treat spent catalysts but report no rhenium recovery.

minerals.name: Selenium
minerals.next_move: Fill Kutch Copper's 150 t/yr selenium capacity and add high-purity refining; India still imports more than it makes.
minerals.what_india_has: About 90 t refined in 2025 from anode slime at Hindalco Dahej and Kutch Copper; 150 t/yr of capacity at Kutch Copper; Hindustan Copper's Ghatsila plant, which last reported selenium in 2006-07.
minerals.cost: Small next to the smelter: Kutch Copper phase 1 cost about US$1.2 bn for 0.5 Mt/yr of copper (#7).

stages.world: A by-product of copper; copper mining is spread (Chile 23%).
stages.india: Arrives in imported copper concentrate.

stages.world: China 2,000 of 3,800 t (2025); Japan 640 t; Russia 320 t.
stages.india: 88 t in 2024 and 90 t in 2025 (USGS). Hindalco refines selenium to over 99% at Dahej; Kutch Copper lists 150 t/yr.

stages.world: High-purity selenium; selenium dioxide; pigments.
stages.india: No high-purity refining reported.

stages.world: Glass, manganese electrolysis, alloys, feed additives, thin-film solar.
stages.india: India imports most of its selenium: 387 t in 2022-23, against exports of 184 t.

minerals.name: Strontium
minerals.next_move: Win customer approvals and fill the new carbonate plant, lock in celestite supply, then move into ferrite magnets.
minerals.what_india_has: Vishnu Chemicals, the first maker of strontium carbonate in India: a plant at Visakhapatnam with about 10,000 t/yr of operating capacity, expandable to 17,000, commercialised in 2025. Celestite ore is imported, now free of customs duty.
minerals.cost: About Rs 110 crore in all: the Rs 52 crore acquisition in 2024 plus later capital spending.

stages.world: Celestite: Iran 250,000 t, Spain 100,000 t, China 80,000 t of 450,000 t (2025).
stages.india: None; celestite is imported.

stages.world: Celestite is converted to strontium carbonate; processing is concentrated in China and Germany.
stages.india: Vishnu Chemicals, Visakhapatnam: about 10,000 t/yr, running at 20 to 25% in early 2026, against Indian demand of about 4,000 t/yr.

stages.world: Strontium ferrite magnets; strontium nitrate.
stages.india: Regular sales, mainly to magnet makers, were expected from early FY27 once customers approved the product.

stages.world: Ferrite magnets, pyrotechnics, drilling fluids, aluminium casting.
stages.india: Demand of about 4,000 t/yr, until now imported, mostly from Mexico and Belgium.

minerals.name: Tellurium
minerals.next_move: Publish and scale Hindalco's copper telluride recovery at Dahej, add a circuit at Kutch Copper, and refine to 5N for cadmium telluride.
minerals.what_india_has: Hindalco's process at Dahej recovers tellurium from slime leachate as copper telluride (no volumes published); Kutch Copper's slime; high-purity tellurium at the Nuclear Fuel Complex; First Solar's 3.3 GW plant as a buyer.
minerals.cost: A circuit is cheap: US$2.9 m for about 20 t/yr at Rio Tinto's Kennecott (#7).

stages.world: A by-product of copper; no primary mines.
stages.india: Arrives in imported copper concentrate.

stages.world: China 800 of 1,000 t (2025); Russia 67 t; Japan 61 t; Sweden 48 t.
stages.india: Copper telluride at Hindalco Dahej. USGS says India may refine some tellurium but has no figures; Hindustan Copper last reported it in 2004-05.

stages.world: 5N to 7N tellurium; cadmium telluride.
stages.india: The Nuclear Fuel Complex makes high-purity tellurium in small lots; none is made into cadmium telluride.

stages.world: Cadmium telluride solar, thermoelectrics, free-machining alloys.
stages.india: First Solar's 3.3 GW plant in Tamil Nadu, which also recovers tellurium from scrap modules; 2 t imported in 2022-23.

chemistry_how.k09: Cadmium telluride needs tellurium of 5N purity or better, a step beyond the copper telluride made at Dahej.
chemistry_how.k10: CSIR-IMMT developed the slime-recovery process that Hindalco lists as implemented.

minerals.name: Tin
minerals.next_move: Work the Chhattisgarh deposits at scale and recover tin from solder and tinplate scrap.
minerals.what_india_has: Small mine output in Dantewada, Chhattisgarh (45 t of concentrate in 2022-23) and one smelter at Jagdalpur (17 t of metal); 103,757 t of contained tin in resources, 64% of the ore in Haryana; a tin block auctioned in Chhattisgarh.

stages.world: China 71,000 t and Indonesia 61,000 t of 290,000 t (2025); Peru, Brazil and DR Congo next.
stages.india: 45,429 kg of concentrate in 2022-23, all from Chhattisgarh; the state corporation buys ore collected by local tribal people.

stages.world: Smelting is simple and widespread.
stages.india: Precious Minerals and Smelting, a joint venture with the state mineral corporation, at Jagdalpur: 17,160 kg of tin metal in 2022-23.

stages.world: Solder, tinplate, tin chemicals.
stages.india: Tinplate (The Tin Plate Company of India, Jamshedpur) and solder, made from imported metal.

stages.world: Electronics solder, food cans, PVC stabilisers.
stages.india: Solder is now the largest use, then tinplate; 13,792 t of tin and alloys were imported in 2022-23.

minerals.name: Beryllium
minerals.next_move: Keep the strategic chain at BARC and draw on the beryl stockpile; for industry, start with beryllium-copper alloy made from imported master alloy.
minerals.what_india_has: BARC's beryllium plant at Vashi, Navi Mumbai, at work since 1982; 4,250 t of beryl stockpiled by the Atomic Minerals Directorate; beryl deposits in five states. Beryllium is a prescribed substance under the Atomic Energy Act, and there is no commercial production.
minerals.cost: No verified plant figure. The US plant built under the Defense Production Act, designed from 2005 under a US$9 m contract, makes 160,000 lb (about 73 t) of high-purity beryllium a year.

stages.world: US 230 of 430 t (2025), from Utah; Brazil 80 t; China 77 t.
stages.india: No commercial production (IBM). Indian beryl holds about 12% beryllium oxide; 4,250 t is stockpiled from prospecting, and export has been banned since independence.

stages.world: Ore to beryllium hydroxide; one US company handles 50 to 70% of the world's processing.
stages.india: BARC extracts beryllium from beryl at Vashi.

stages.world: Metal, oxide and beryllium-copper master alloy.
stages.india: BARC makes beryllium metal parts such as X-ray windows and rods by powder metallurgy.

stages.world: Consumer electronics 29%, aerospace and defence 24%, industrial components 17% (US, by sales).
stages.india: Space, defence and nuclear programmes; imports worth Rs 3.67 crore in 2022-23.

minerals.name: Hafnium
minerals.next_move: Scale C-MET's hafnium sponge pilot on the Nuclear Fuel Complex's raffinate, and add crystal-bar refining.
minerals.what_india_has: The Nuclear Fuel Complex strips hafnium from zirconium for reactor tubes; IREL has made 99% hafnium oxide from that raffinate; C-MET and VSSC run a 320 kg/yr sponge pilot.

stages.world: Inside zircon: Australia 33% and South Africa 23% of zircon output (2025).
stages.india: IREL and KMML recover zircon, but most zircon is imported.

stages.world: Hafnium is separated only where nuclear-grade zirconium is made: France, the US, Russia, China.
stages.india: NFC removes hafnium by solvent extraction in its nuclear zirconium chain.

stages.world: Hafnium sponge and crystal bar.
stages.india: C-MET and VSSC pilot: 320 kg/yr of sponge.

stages.world: Superalloys (the leading use), reactor control rods, chip gate oxides.
stages.india: Space and nuclear programmes.

minerals.name: Indium
minerals.next_move: Assay Hindustan Zinc's residues for indium, and pilot CSIR-NML's recovery of indium from scrap display panels.
minerals.value_chain_step: Indium recovery from zinc residues and scrap
minerals.what_india_has: Large zinc smelters with no indium circuit (IBM records no production). CSIR-NML has a laboratory process that recovers about 97% of the indium from scrap LCD panels; the Nuclear Fuel Complex developed high-purity indium and passed the technology to industry.

stages.world: A by-product of zinc; zinc deposits hold under 1 to 100 parts per million.
stages.india: Hindustan Zinc mines zinc at scale; no indium grades are published for its ores.

stages.world: China 760 of 1,100 t (2025); South Korea 180 t, where Korea Zinc makes about 150 t a year; Japan 65 t.
stages.india: None (IBM). CSIR-NML's process for scrap LCD panels awaits a pilot trial.

stages.world: Indium tin oxide sputtering targets; indium phosphide.
stages.india: The Nuclear Fuel Complex developed high-purity indium technology; no commercial output.

stages.world: Flat-panel displays, solders, thin-film solar, photonics chips.
stages.india: Display and electronics makers; all imported.

minerals.name: Platinum
minerals.next_move: Grow recycling: secure spent catalysts and scrapped converters for Indian refiners, and assess the Boula-Nuasahi deposit.
minerals.what_india_has: Hindustan Platinum (founded 1961) refines platinum, palladium, rhodium, ruthenium and iridium from spent catalysts and says it is at peak production; Ravindra Heraeus recycles catalysts at Udaipur; Johnson Matthey (Manesar) and BASF (Chennai) coat autocatalysts in India; a Rs 1,500 crore recycling scheme covers catalytic converters. Resources of 20.92 t of platinum-group metals, 67% in Odisha.

stages.world: South Africa 120 of 170 t (2025); Russia 20 t; Zimbabwe 18 t.
stages.india: None. Boula-Nuasahi in Odisha is the only proven deposit.

stages.world: Smelters and precious-metal refineries beside the mines in South Africa and Russia; recyclers elsewhere.
stages.india: Hindustan Platinum and Ravindra Heraeus refine spent catalysts.

stages.world: Autocatalysts, chemical catalysts, alloys.
stages.india: Johnson Matthey (Manesar, 25 million autocatalysts made by 2014) and BASF (Chennai) coat autocatalysts with imported metal.

stages.world: Catalytic converters, jewellery, chemical and glass plant, hydrogen fuel cells.
stages.india: Primary metal is entirely imported (IBM); vehicle catalysts and jewellery.

chemistry_how.k08: Spent refinery and chemical catalysts are the main feed for India's platinum-group refiners.

minerals.name: Palladium
minerals.next_move: Grow recycling: secure spent catalysts and scrapped converters for Indian refiners, and assess the Boula-Nuasahi deposit.
minerals.what_india_has: Hindustan Platinum (founded 1961) refines platinum, palladium, rhodium, ruthenium and iridium from spent catalysts and says it is at peak production; Ravindra Heraeus recycles catalysts at Udaipur; Johnson Matthey (Manesar) and BASF (Chennai) coat autocatalysts in India; a Rs 1,500 crore recycling scheme covers catalytic converters. Resources of 20.92 t of platinum-group metals, 67% in Odisha.

stages.world: Russia 84 of 190 t (2025); South Africa 70 t; Canada 16 t; Zimbabwe 15 t.
stages.india: None. Boula-Nuasahi in Odisha is the only proven deposit.

stages.world: Smelters and precious-metal refineries beside the mines in South Africa and Russia; recyclers elsewhere.
stages.india: Hindustan Platinum and Ravindra Heraeus refine spent catalysts.

stages.world: Autocatalysts, chemical catalysts, alloys.
stages.india: Johnson Matthey (Manesar, 25 million autocatalysts made by 2014) and BASF (Chennai) coat autocatalysts with imported metal.

stages.world: Petrol-car catalytic converters, electronics, dentistry.
stages.india: Primary metal is entirely imported (IBM); vehicle catalysts and electronics.

chemistry_how.k08: Spent refinery and chemical catalysts are the main feed for India's platinum-group refiners.

minerals.name: Rhodium
minerals.next_move: Grow recycling: secure spent catalysts and scrapped converters for Indian refiners, and assess the Boula-Nuasahi deposit.
minerals.what_india_has: Hindustan Platinum (founded 1961) refines platinum, palladium, rhodium, ruthenium and iridium from spent catalysts and says it is at peak production; Ravindra Heraeus recycles catalysts at Udaipur; Johnson Matthey (Manesar) and BASF (Chennai) coat autocatalysts in India; a Rs 1,500 crore recycling scheme covers catalytic converters. Resources of 20.92 t of platinum-group metals, 67% in Odisha.

stages.world: A by-product of platinum mining; South Africa has more than 85%.
stages.india: None. Boula-Nuasahi in Odisha is the only proven deposit.

stages.world: Smelters and precious-metal refineries beside the mines in South Africa and Russia; recyclers elsewhere.
stages.india: Hindustan Platinum and Ravindra Heraeus refine spent catalysts.

stages.world: Autocatalysts, chemical catalysts, alloys.
stages.india: Johnson Matthey (Manesar, 25 million autocatalysts made by 2014) and BASF (Chennai) coat autocatalysts with imported metal.

stages.world: Catalytic converters, almost entirely.
stages.india: Imported, for vehicle and chemical catalysts.

chemistry_how.k08: Spent refinery and chemical catalysts are the main feed for India's platinum-group refiners.

minerals.name: Ruthenium
minerals.next_move: Grow recycling: secure spent catalysts and scrapped converters for Indian refiners, and assess the Boula-Nuasahi deposit.
minerals.what_india_has: Hindustan Platinum (founded 1961) refines platinum, palladium, rhodium, ruthenium and iridium from spent catalysts and says it is at peak production; Ravindra Heraeus recycles catalysts at Udaipur; Johnson Matthey (Manesar) and BASF (Chennai) coat autocatalysts in India; a Rs 1,500 crore recycling scheme covers catalytic converters. Resources of 20.92 t of platinum-group metals, 67% in Odisha.

stages.world: A by-product of platinum mining; South Africa has more than 85%.
stages.india: None. Boula-Nuasahi in Odisha is the only proven deposit.

stages.world: Smelters and precious-metal refineries beside the mines in South Africa and Russia; recyclers elsewhere.
stages.india: Hindustan Platinum and Ravindra Heraeus refine spent catalysts.

stages.world: Autocatalysts, chemical catalysts, alloys.
stages.india: Hindustan Platinum also manufactures precious-metal products.

stages.world: Hard disks, chip resistors, chemical catalysts.
stages.india: Imported; 890 kg of iridium, osmium and ruthenium came in during 2022-23.

chemistry_how.k08: Spent refinery and chemical catalysts are the main feed for India's platinum-group refiners.

minerals.name: Iridium
minerals.next_move: Recycle iridium from catalysts and crucibles now, and from electrolysers as green hydrogen scales.
minerals.what_india_has: Hindustan Platinum (founded 1961) refines platinum, palladium, rhodium, ruthenium and iridium from spent catalysts and says it is at peak production; Ravindra Heraeus recycles catalysts at Udaipur; Johnson Matthey (Manesar) and BASF (Chennai) coat autocatalysts in India; a Rs 1,500 crore recycling scheme covers catalytic converters. Resources of 20.92 t of platinum-group metals, 67% in Odisha.

stages.world: A by-product of platinum mining; South Africa has more than 85%.
stages.india: None. Boula-Nuasahi in Odisha is the only proven deposit.

stages.world: Smelters and precious-metal refineries beside the mines in South Africa and Russia; recyclers elsewhere.
stages.india: Hindustan Platinum and Ravindra Heraeus refine spent catalysts.

stages.world: Autocatalysts, chemical catalysts, alloys.
stages.india: Hindustan Platinum also manufactures precious-metal products.

stages.world: Electrolyser anodes, crucibles for crystal growing, spark plugs.
stages.india: Imported; the green hydrogen mission will need it for PEM electrolysers.

chemistry_how.k08: Spent refinery and chemical catalysts are the main feed for India's platinum-group refiners.

minerals.name: Tantalum
minerals.next_move: Scale the Nuclear Fuel Complex's tantalum line on stockpiled and imported concentrate, and recover tantalum from capacitor scrap.
minerals.what_india_has: The Nuclear Fuel Complex makes tantalum pentoxide and tantalum metal and developed capacitor-grade powder and anodes; VSSC's niobium facility there processes columbite-tantalite by solvent extraction; the Atomic Minerals Directorate holds 149 t of columbite-tantalite. No commercial mining (IBM).

stages.world: DR Congo 1,300 of 2,500 t (2025); Rwanda 400 t; Nigeria 390 t; Brazil 190 t.
stages.india: No commercial production (IBM). 149 t of columbite-tantalite is stockpiled from prospecting; a tantalum exploration block in Maharashtra was annulled.

stages.world: Acid digestion and solvent extraction to part tantalum from niobium; China is the largest processor, with about 43%.
stages.india: Solvent extraction of tantalum and niobium at the Nuclear Fuel Complex, at small scale.

stages.world: Capacitor powder, sputtering targets, mill products.
stages.india: NFC makes tantalum pentoxide and tantalum metal, and passed capacitor-grade powder and anode technology to industry.

stages.world: Capacitors, chips, superalloys, chemical plant.
stages.india: Electronics and semiconductor demand, imported.

minerals.name: Cerium
minerals.next_move: Use the surplus: make polishing powder and catalyst-grade ceria in India from IREL and Toyotsu oxide.
minerals.what_india_has: IREL separates cerium oxide of over 99% purity at Aluva and is India's only monazite processor; Toyotsu refines cerium at Visakhapatnam. IBM lists cerium among the rare earths India has in surplus, and IREL calls the home market for its rare-earth products almost non-existent.

stages.world: China 270,000 of 390,000 t of rare-earth oxide (2025); US 51,000 t. Cerium is the most plentiful rare earth.
stages.india: 2,900 t of rare-earth oxide in 2025, from monazite.

stages.world: China does about 91% of rare-earth separation.
stages.india: IREL (Aluva) and Toyotsu (Visakhapatnam) separate cerium; India refined 2,000 t of rare-earth oxide against 5,000 t of capacity (IBM).

stages.world: Polishing powder, catalyst washcoat, glass additives, mischmetal.
stages.india: IREL's Bhopal park has a mini-plant that demonstrates cerium metal.

stages.world: Glass polishing, catalytic converters, refinery catalysts.
stages.india: Little home demand yet; much rare-earth output is exported. IBM says capacity to consume the light rare earths is being built.

minerals.name: Lanthanum
minerals.next_move: Turn surplus lanthanum into cracking-catalyst additives for India's refineries.
minerals.what_india_has: IREL separates lanthanum oxide of over 99% purity at Aluva; Toyotsu refines lanthanum at Visakhapatnam. IBM lists lanthanum among the rare earths India has in surplus, and IREL calls the home market for its rare-earth products almost non-existent.

stages.world: China 270,000 of 390,000 t of rare-earth oxide (2025); US 51,000 t.
stages.india: 2,900 t of rare-earth oxide in 2025, from monazite.

stages.world: China does about 91% of rare-earth separation.
stages.india: IREL (Aluva) and Toyotsu (Visakhapatnam) separate lanthanum.

stages.world: Cracking catalysts, nickel-metal-hydride alloys, optical glass.
stages.india: IREL's Bhopal park has a mini-plant that demonstrates lanthanum metal.

stages.world: Oil refining, hybrid-car batteries, camera lenses.
stages.india: Little home demand yet; much rare-earth output is exported. IBM says capacity to consume the light rare earths is being built.

minerals.name: Europium
minerals.next_move: No large move: demand has shrunk as LEDs replaced fluorescent lamps. Keep small-scale separation at IREL.
minerals.what_india_has: IREL lists europium oxide of over 99% purity among its Aluva products. IBM notes that europium is not present in Indian deposits in extractable quantity.

stages.world: A minor part of all rare-earth ores; China 270,000 of 390,000 t of rare-earth oxide (2025).
stages.india: Traces in monazite.

stages.world: China does about 91% of rare-earth separation.
stages.india: Small quantities at IREL, Aluva.

stages.world: Red and blue phosphors.
stages.india: None.

stages.world: Lighting and display phosphors, security inks.
stages.india: Small; imported.

minerals.name: Niobium
minerals.next_move: Prove up the niobium found with rare earths in Gujarat and Rajasthan, and scale the Nuclear Fuel Complex's niobium line.
minerals.what_india_has: 142,200 t of niobium oxide in hard-rock rare-earth deposits of Gujarat and Rajasthan (Atomic Minerals Directorate); auctioned blocks in Rajasthan; the Nuclear Fuel Complex makes reactor-grade and superconductor-grade niobium, and VSSC's 3 t/yr niobium thermit facility there serves the space programme.
minerals.cost: A new mine and plant is large: NioCorp's Elk Creek project in Nebraska is put at about US$1.85 bn.

stages.india: No production (IBM). 142,200 t of niobium oxide established in Gujarat and Rajasthan; the Bhatikhera and Southeast of Gugrot blocks have preferred bidders.

stages.world: Pyrochlore concentrate is reduced with aluminium to ferroniobium beside the mine.
stages.india: Small-scale separation from columbite-tantalite at the Nuclear Fuel Complex.

stages.world: Mostly ferroniobium for steel; niobium alloys and superconducting wire.
stages.india: NFC makes reactor-grade niobium for zirconium alloys and high-purity niobium for superconductors; niobium thermit, 3 t/yr, for satellite thrusters. No ferroniobium.

stages.world: Steels 77%, superalloys 23% (US).
stages.india: Imported 5,245 t of ferroniobium in 2022-23, mainly through Singapore and from Brazil.

minerals.name: Osmium
minerals.next_move: No capability move is warranted: the market is laboratory-scale.
minerals.what_india_has: None specific to osmium. The metals Hindustan Platinum reports recovering do not include it.

stages.world: A by-product of platinum mining; South Africa has more than 85%.
stages.india: None.

stages.world: Distilled off as osmium tetroxide in precious-metal refineries.
stages.india: None reported.

stages.world: Osmium tetroxide; hard alloys.
stages.india: None.

stages.world: Microscopy stains, chemical catalysts, instrument tips.
stages.india: Imported in very small quantities; 890 kg of iridium, osmium and ruthenium together in 2022-23.

minerals.name: Vanadium
minerals.next_move: Recover vanadium from what India already processes: Bayer sludge at alumina refineries, steel slag, refinery petcoke and spent catalysts.
minerals.value_chain_step: Vanadium from sludge, slag and refinery residues
minerals.what_india_has: Vanadium sludge at alumina refineries (BALCO 6 to 10% V2O5, Hindalco Renukoot 8.2%); recovery processes at Vedanta Lanjigarh, NALCO (lab) and Reliance (gasifier slag, lab to pilot); 839 t of ferro-vanadium made in 2022-23.

stages.world: China 82,000 of 110,000 t (2025); Russia 21,000 t; Brazil and South Africa about 5,000 t each.
stages.india: None. Resources of 24.63 Mt of ore holding 64,594 t of V2O5 (IBM), and 81,300 t of vanadium oxide with hard-rock rare earths (Atomic Minerals Directorate); graphite-vanadium blocks auctioned in Arunachal Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.

stages.world: Steel slag is salt-roasted and leached to vanadium pentoxide; China dominant.
stages.india: Vanadium sludge from Bayer liquor at BALCO, Hindalco and Vedanta; Reliance and VFlowTech with IIT Delhi are developing recovery from refinery residues.

stages.world: Ferrovanadium; electrolyte for flow batteries.
stages.india: 839 t of ferro-vanadium in 2022-23, against imports of 1,211 t.

stages.world: Steel (over 90% in the US), titanium alloys, catalysts, flow batteries.
stages.india: Steelmakers; NTPC's 100 MWh vanadium flow battery at Khavda.

chemistry_how.k08: Spent refinery catalysts and petcoke carry vanadium alongside molybdenum and nickel.

minerals.name: Promethium
minerals.next_move: None warranted. If a need arose, production would sit with the atomic-energy establishment's reactors and hot cells.
minerals.what_india_has: No production. BARC developed promethium-147 sources for a coating-thickness gauge at the Nuclear Fuel Complex in 2009, and its reactors and radiochemistry laboratories make medical isotopes.

stages.world: Not mined: every isotope is radioactive and short-lived.
stages.india: None.

stages.world: Made in reactors and separated in hot cells; the US DOE Isotope Program is the only global producer of promethium-147.
stages.india: None.

stages.world: Promethium-147 salts and sealed sources.
stages.india: BARC has fabricated promethium-147 sources (2009).

stages.world: Nuclear batteries, thickness gauges, luminous paint.
stages.india: A coating-thickness gauge at the Nuclear Fuel Complex.
